definitions.title: Function of Two or Three Variables
definitions.latex: z = f(x, y), \quad w = f(x, y, z)
definitions.statement: A real-valued function of two variables f is a rule that assigns a unique real number z to each ordered pair (x, y) in a subset D of R^2 called the domain. The set of all resulting output values is the range.
conditions: Domain D is a subset of R^2 (or R^n)
Range is a subset of R
definitions.explanation: The graph of z = f(x, y) is a surface S in Euclidean 3-space consisting of all points (x, y, f(x, y)) for (x, y) in D.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Generalizes single-variable curves to surfaces and scalar fields in higher dimensions.

definitions.title: Level Curves and Level Surfaces
definitions.latex: f(x, y) = c, \quad f(x, y, z) = c
definitions.statement: The level curves of a function of two variables f(x, y) are the curves in the xy-plane with equations f(x, y) = c, where c is a constant in the range of f. For three variables, f(x, y, z) = c forms level surfaces in R^3.
conditions: Constant c is in the range of f
definitions.explanation: Analogous to contour lines on a topographical map, level curves show where the function maintains constant height or potential.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Level curves map 3D surfaces onto 2D contour representations.
